steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Composition is the arrangement of visual elements within the picture plane — it guides the viewer's eye and creates meaning.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The rule of thirds divides the image into nine sections; placing focal points at intersections creates dynamic balance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Negative space (the empty areas) is as important as positive space — it defines shapes and creates breathing room.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Foreground, middle ground and background create depth and lead the viewer into the picture.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring composition and layout. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with composition and layout. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with composition and layout. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to composition and layout, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes. | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
